## Discipline (applies to every source)

- **Fire research early, in parallel** with your first code reads — it costs
  almost no wall-clock and stops you building on a wrong assumption.
- **Triangulate.** Any claim that drives a decision gets confirmed across ≥2
  independent sources. Code tells you *what*; Unblocked/Slack/PRs tell you *why*.
- **Cite.** Keep the URL, PR number, `file:line`, or verbatim quote so a
  reviewer can check your reasoning — and so you can.
- **Three buckets, kept distinct:** stated fact · labeled inference · unknown.
  Never let an inference harden into a "fact."
- **Ask, don't assume.** When a material fact is missing and no tool can supply
  it, ask the user a specific question rather than inventing an answer.
- **Multi-modal.** One search angle is not enough. A local grep miss may just
  mean the code lives in an associated repo — try Unblocked code search before

# Unblocked Sync

Woods pushes condensed Markdown profiles of extracted units to an
[Unblocked](https://getunblocked.com) collection via its Documents API.
User-facing reference: `docs/UNBLOCKED_INTEGRATION.md`. This skill is the
agent-facing operational map.

## Components (`lib/woods/unblocked/`)

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `client.rb` | Net::HTTP REST client. `put_document` (upsert by URI), `delete_document`, `list_documents`/`all_documents` (paginated, no body returned), `create_collection`/`list_collections`. Raises `ApiError < Woods::Error` carrying the HTTP `status`. |
| `document_builder.rb` | Unit JSON → `{title:, body:, uri:}` Markdown. **Every rendered collection is sorted** — body bytes must be a function of content, not input order, because the exporter hashes them. Credential-scrubs bodies (fails closed to empty string). |
| `exporter.rb` | Orchestrates the sync. Skip-if-unchanged via manifest hash, reconcile-on-empty-manifest, orphan purge with safety guards. |
| `sync_manifest.rb` | JSON at `<output_dir>/unblocked_sync_manifest.json`: `uri → {hash, document_id}`. Atomic save; discards itself on collection-id mismatch or corrupt file (degrades to full re-push). |
| `rate_limiter.rb` | 1000-calls/day budget (override: `UNBLOCKED_DAILY_BUDGET`). Raises `BudgetExhaustedError < Woods::Error` when spent. |

## Setup (one-time per host app)

1. Team API token: Unblocked web app → Settings → API Tokens.
2. Create the collection **via the API** (no UI path):
   ```ruby
   client = Woods::Unblocked::Client.new(api_token: ENV['UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN'])
   client.create_collection(name: '...', description: '...')['id']
   ```
   `iconUrl` defaults to `Client::DEFAULT_ICON_URL` (the repo-hosted Woods
   mark). **The live API 400s without an iconUrl** even though its docs say
   optional — never strip the default.
3. Set `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN`, `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID`, `UNBLOCKED_REPO_URL`
   (env vars override `Woods.configure` values in the rake task).
4. Run `bin/rails woods:extract` then `bin/rails woods:unblocked_sync`
   (alias: `woods:relay`).

## How incremental sync decides

- **Skip:** SHA256 of built `title + "\n" + body` matches the manifest entry.
- **Push:** hash differs or URI unknown. `put_document` upserts by URI.
- **Delete:** manifest URIs absent from the current run's full unit set
  (partial-sync types track ALL existing units, so a poro falling out of the
  top-100 is *not* a deletion).
- **Reconcile:** empty manifest → one paginated `all_documents` sweep seeds
  `document_id`s (hash stays nil → full re-push, but orphan purge still works).

### Purge safety rails (both intentional — do not "fix")

- Budget exhausted mid-run → purge skipped entirely (current set incomplete).
- Mass-deletion guard: refuses to delete >30% of a ≥10-doc manifest unless
  `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_PURGE=1`. Triggers when someone syncs a partial index
  (e.g. `woods:incremental` output in a fresh directory).

## Escape hatches (truthy: `1`/`true`/`yes`, case-insensitive)

- `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_FULL_SYNC` — re-push everything, ignoring the unchanged
  check. Use after a `DocumentBuilder` format change to make intent explicit
  (every body hash shifts anyway, so the effect is the same either way).
- `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_PURGE` — bypass the mass-deletion guard. **This is the flag
  a `unblocked_repo_url` change needs:** every URI changes, so everything
  re-pushes on its own (all URIs are new to the manifest), but the old-URI
  documents become 100% of the stale set — which trips the >30% guard — and
  they persist as remote duplicates until a run with FORCE_PURGE deletes them.

## Symptom → cause

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---------|--------------|
| Everything re-pushes every run | Manifest not persisted between CI runs (cache restore missing), OR a `DocumentBuilder` change altered all bodies, OR nondeterministic body output (unsorted collection — check any new `build_*` method) |
| `0 synced, N skipped`, but docs stale in Unblocked | Hash matched stale manifest from another checkout — delete the manifest to force reconcile |
| A few units re-push every warm run; manifest entry count < synced | Multiple units share one `file_path` (nested/namespaced classes, several classes per `.rb`). `build_uri_index` disambiguates them (`?unit=` suffix on all but the lexically-first identifier) — if it regresses, those units collide on one URI again |
| A unit's document is missing from the collection (only one of N co-located classes present) | Same file-sharing collision overwriting on a shared URI — `build_uri_index` is the fix |
| `WARNING: refusing to delete X of Y documents` | Partial index — sync against full extraction output. Or an *intentional* large removal (type dropped from FULL_SYNC_TYPES, `unblocked_repo_url` change, big deletion): re-run once with `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_PURGE=1` |
| `daily budget exhausted` | >1000 calls today. Cold start needs ~1005 for ~1000 docs; converges next run. Raise `UNBLOCKED_DAILY_BUDGET` only if the plan allows |
| Bare `400 Bad Request` on create_collection | Missing `iconUrl` (live-API quirk) |
| `TypeError` parsing list responses | Live API returns bare JSON arrays, not `{items:}` envelopes — guard with `is_a?(Array)` first |

## Working on this code

- **TDD per repo conventions.** Exporter specs use a `manifest_double` helper;
  client specs stub `Net::HTTP` (see `stub_http_sequence`).
- **Determinism is a hard invariant:** any new `DocumentBuilder` output must be
  byte-identical across runs for unchanged input — extend the order-independence
  spec in `spec/unblocked/document_builder_spec.rb` when adding sections.
- Error classes: raise/rescue `ApiError` (required `status`) for HTTP failures;
  `BudgetExhaustedError` for budget stops — detected in `note_budget_exhaustion`
  (single chokepoint; class check with a message-text fallback).
- **Live smoke** (writes to the real org, self-cleaning): create temp collection
  → put → `all_documents` → delete doc → delete collection. Needs the
  Team token. Pattern: `script` it against `Client` directly; never log the token.
- Concurrency: the gem does not lock the manifest — CI must serialize sync runs
  (Buildkite `concurrency_group` / GHA `concurrency:`).

# Woods → Unblocked: Structural Context for Code Review

> Destined for Notion once the pipeline has run in production for a while; lives
> here so it can be reviewed alongside the implementing PR (#13304, ENG-5434).

We feed Unblocked's automated PR reviewer factual, machine-extracted knowledge
of this codebase — model associations, dependent counts, blast radius, entry
points, side effects — so reviews can flag impact *outside* the diff (e.g. "this
changes a model with 127 dependents and 5 triggered workers; none of their tests
changed"). A scheduled Buildkite build extracts ~6,500 code units with the
[woods gem](https://github.com/lost-in-the/woods) and syncs condensed Markdown
profiles into the **"Admin Woods"** Unblocked collection via its Documents API
(incremental as of woods 1.4.0 — only changed docs each run). The same
extraction powers local Woods MCP servers for developer agent sessions. Main
risks: API budget on a cold/cache-miss run (~800–1,200 calls ≈ the default
daily limit; steady state is ~0) and document staleness between syncs (profiles
lag main by up to a day).

## How it works

```
nightly Buildkite build (main)
  └─ rails ci:setup                 # prepared DB — extraction introspects schema
  └─ rails woods:extract            # ~6,559 units → tmp/woods/ (JSON + Markdown)
  └─ rails woods:unblocked_sync     # ~800–1,200 docs → Unblocked Documents API
                                    #   upsert by URI (GitHub blob links)
Unblocked indexes the collection (~1 min)
  └─ PR reviews cite Admin Woods profiles for blast radius / entry points
  └─ Q&A / PR Chat answers ground in the same profiles
```

- **Extraction** runs inside Rails (runtime introspection, not static parsing):
  associations, callbacks, dependency graph (8,286 edges as of 2026-06-10),
  PageRank-style importance scores. Output: `tmp/woods/`.
- **Sync** is gem-native (`woods:unblocked_sync`) and **incremental** as of
  woods 1.4.0: a `SyncManifest` (`tmp/woods/unblocked_sync_manifest.json`)
  records the content hash + remote id of everything last pushed, so each run
  only PUTs new/changed documents, deletes documents whose unit disappeared,
  and skips the rest. Documents are keyed by URI — the GitHub blob URL of the
  source file — so a missing manifest (first run, CI cache miss) degrades to a
  correct full re-push that rebuilds it. Steady state on an unchanged codebase
  costs ~0 API calls. `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_FULL_SYNC=1` bypasses the skip.
- **What syncs** (`Woods::Unblocked::Exporter`): all models, controllers,
  services, jobs, mailers, managers, decorators, concerns, serializers, and
  GraphQL types/mutations/resolvers/queries; plus the top 100 POROs and top 50
  libs by dependent count. Roughly 800–1,200 documents for this app.

## Setup (one-time)

A working pipeline needs **both** the collection (the data) and the Code Review
config (the behavior). In order:

1. **Create the "Admin Woods" collection.** In Unblocked: Settings → Data
   Sources → Add Data Sources → **Create a Custom Source**, name it
   "Admin Woods." Copy its ID — that's `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID`. The sync
   pushes into an existing collection; it does **not** create one, so this must
   exist first. Suggested prompt description (helps Unblocked reference the
   content accurately):

   > Machine-generated structural profiles of the Big Cartel admin Rails
   > codebase, extracted from the running application by the Woods gem and
   > refreshed from the main branch. Each document profiles one code unit — a
   > model, controller, service, job, mailer, GraphQL type/mutation/resolver,
   > concern, serializer, decorator, or significant plain Ruby object —
   > summarizing its associations, dependent count and blast radius, entry
   > points (controllers, GraphQL resolvers, and jobs that reference it), schema
   > highlights (enums, scopes, callbacks), and side effects (background workers
   > and mailers it triggers). Document URIs link to the source file on GitHub.
   > Use these to assess the impact of a change beyond the diff: which callers,
   > jobs, and mailers a unit touches, and how structurally central it is.

   Store the collection's ID in the **"Unblocked - Admin Woods API Token"**
   1Password item, in the `collection_id` field (alongside the token).
2. **Create a team/org-level API token.** Unblocked → Settings → API Tokens
   (a team token, not personal — higher budget, shared). It lives in the same
   1Password item ("Unblocked - Admin Woods API Token"). So that one item is
   the source of truth for both values — the token *and* `collection_id`.
3. **Register Buildkite agent env** (DevOps), both read from the 1Password item
   above: `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` (the token field) and `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID`
   (the `collection_id` field). They reach the container through the
   `.buildkite/ci-compose.yml` allowlist — the same path `RAILS_MASTER_KEY`
   uses. Don't interpolate them in pipeline YAML (it bakes the value into the
   uploaded pipeline); the allowlist already forwards them.
4. **Create the Buildkite schedule** (pipeline settings → New schedule,
   `branch: main`, off-peak UTC). The sync step is gated
   `build.source == "schedule"`, so it only fires on the schedule.
5. **Code Review settings** (Unblocked → Code Review):
   - **Repository Instructions = ON** — *required.* This is what makes the
     reviewer read `AGENTS.md` / `.claude/rules/`; without it the steering below
     does nothing.
   - **Risk Assessment** — automatic from `.unblocked/risk-policies.yaml` once
     merged to main (read from the default branch). No UI step for the
     policies themselves.
   - **Risk-based auto-approval = OFF** (it's a separate, optional toggle from
     Risk Assessment). Every PR still gets a scored risk report; leaving
     auto-approval off keeps current review behavior exactly as-is while
     scores accumulate. Revisit after a few weeks once the reports confirm
     `low` lands where a human would also say "routine".
   - **Approvals = Comment** (not Approve — see the auto-approve note in
     Operations), **Review draft PRs = OFF**, **PR Descriptions = OFF**,
     **Excluded Paths** = vendored/generated only (**not** `db/structure.sql`).
6. **First sync** — run `woods:extract` + `woods:unblocked_sync` once manually
   (token from 1Password), then again immediately; the second run should report
   `synced ~0 / skipped ~all`, confirming the manifest and incremental path
   end-to-end before the schedule takes over.

## Steering the reviewer

Two independent things must both be in place: the **collection** (the data —
synced by the pipeline above) and the **instructions** (telling the reviewer to
use it). The instructions live in the repo and are picked up only when
Unblocked's **Repository Instructions** toggle is ON (Code Review settings →
Custom Rules → "Follow CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md … found in your repository").

- **Required toggle:** Repository Instructions = **ON**. With it off, Unblocked
  ignores `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/rules/` entirely and none of the steering
  below applies — the collection is still indexed, but the reviewer is never
  told to prefer it.
- **In-repo (correctly scoped to admin):**
  [`.claude/rules/woods-unblocked.md`](../.claude/rules/woods-unblocked.md)
  holds the full guidance (review heuristics + local agent usage); `AGENTS.md`
  carries a one-line pointer in the Guardrails list to keep it concise.
- **Global Instructions** in Unblocked apply org-wide (every repo), so the
  admin-specific Woods steering does **not** belong there — keep it repo-level.
  Leave Global Instructions for genuinely cross-repo standards; revisit only if
  Woods extends to other repos.

## Local developer usage

Most developers have Unblocked access, so the profiles are queryable in any
agent session via the Unblocked MCP (`context_research` naming a model:
"what's the blast radius of changing Order?"). For richer/offline queries, two
local MCP servers target the dev containers — registered in this repo's
`.mcp.json` and launched by `bin/woods-start` / `bin/woods-console-start`:

| Server | Data | Setup | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `woods-admin` | Static index (`tmp/woods/`) | `bin/rails woods:extract` once per worktree | lookups, dependents, blast radius, flow traces |
| `woods-admin-console` | Live Rails (dev DB) | none | current schema, association traversal, row counts |
| `unblocked` | Admin Woods collection + org knowledge | Unblocked CLI auth | profiles as of last nightly sync + PRs/Slack/Linear |

Agents pick this up without a walkthrough: the `querying-codebase-structure`
project skill (`.claude/skills/`) routes structural questions ("blast radius
of X", "who depends on X") to the right server automatically, and
`.claude/rules/woods-unblocked.md` carries the full guidance for review
agents.

## Operations

| Concern | Current state |
|---|---|
| Cadence | Nightly Buildkite schedule on main (`if: build.source == "schedule"` gate in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`). Schedule itself is created in Buildkite pipeline settings. |
| Secrets | `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` (team/org-level key), `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID` — registered as Buildkite agent env (DevOps), forwarded to the container via the allowlist in `.buildkite/ci-compose.yml`. |
| API budget | Default 1,000 calls/day (`UNBLOCKED_DAILY_BUDGET` overrides). A full sync (first run or manifest cache-miss) is ~800–1,200 calls; the rate limiter stops gracefully at the budget and idempotent re-runs converge. With the sync manifest restored across runs, steady state is ~0 calls — but until the manifest restore step exists in CI (ENG-5462), every nightly run is a cache-miss full sync. |
| Failure mode | `soft_fail: true` until two consecutive green scheduled runs; the step can never block merges either way (schedule-only). Note: as of woods 1.4.0 the rake task exits 1 on sync errors (except budget exhaustion with partial progress) — currently masked by `soft_fail`, and exactly the signal we want once it comes off. |
| Deletions | The sync deletes remote documents whose source unit disappeared. A mass-deletion guard refuses to purge >30% of the manifest (signature of a partial index — but also fires on intentional large removals); override with `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_PURGE=1`. |
| Risk Assessment | `.unblocked/risk-policies.yaml` (read from the default branch) scores each PR after a clean review; anything unmatched defaults to low. **Risk-based auto-approval is a separate, optional toggle — currently recommended OFF**, so scores are report-only and review behavior is unchanged. If enabled later: `low`/`lowest` auto-approves; policies are scoped so sensitive changes (auth, payments, migrations, hot models, public API, review/CI config) score medium+ and never auto-approve; and if branch protection counts Unblocked's approval toward required reviews, routine PRs may merge without a human — enable knowingly. |
| Gem loading | `gem 'woods'` is in `group :development, :test`. The initializer guards on `defined?(Woods)`. Production never loads it. |
| Rollback | Remove the pipeline step (or delete the Buildkite schedule) — no app code paths depend on the sync. Stale documents persist in Unblocked until deleted from the collection or overwritten. |

## Phase 2 (not yet implemented)

- **Manifest restore in CI (ENG-5462).** The sync is incremental as of woods
  1.4.0, but ephemeral CI containers start without the previous run's
  `unblocked_sync_manifest.json` — so every scheduled run is a cache-miss full
  re-push until we restore it. The manifest already uploads with the step's
  `artifact_paths: tmp/woods/**/*`; the missing half is downloading it from
  the last successful scheduled build (Buildkite API token required, or the
  S3-backed cache plugin). Once restored, steady state is ~0 API calls —
  which also reopens the **per-merge vs nightly cadence** decision; gate with
  a Buildkite `concurrency_group` if moving to per-merge (concurrent syncs
  can interleave manifest writes).
- **Incremental extraction.** `woods:incremental` re-extracts only units
  affected by changed files but needs the previous `dependency_graph.json`
  restored the same way. Saves extraction minutes only (the sync already
  skips unchanged docs via the manifest) — worthwhile if extraction time
  grows or per-merge freshness lands.
- **Hosted Woods MCP (production access).** Explicitly deferred until a
  secure-access design is approved by DevOps: token scheme, network placement,
  and the console MCP staying dev-only. Woods 1.3.0's `:shared_filesystem`
  preset (embed artifacts on disk, separate MCP process) is the likely shape.
- **Semantic search.** The local MCP currently runs pattern search
  (`WOODS_ALLOW_AUTODETECT=1`). Configuring an embedding provider (Ollama) and
  running `woods:embed` enables semantic retrieval; not part of the standard
  dev setup yet.

## Gotchas

- **Extraction needs a prepared database** — it introspects the schema. The CI
  step runs `rails ci:setup` first; locally use a worktree whose container has
  the dev DB (`bin/rails woods:extract` inside the right container — check
  which worktree `bc_admin` mounts before trusting results).
- **The CI env allowlist eats unknown vars.** `UNBLOCKED_*` must be listed
  under the admin service in `.buildkite/ci-compose.yml` or the container
  silently sees nothing.
- **The collection must exist first.** `woods:unblocked_sync` pushes into the
  collection named by `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID` and does not create it — a
  missing or wrong ID is the most likely "ran it, nothing appeared." Create the
  custom source in Unblocked first (see Setup).
- **Repository Instructions must be ON in Unblocked**, or the reviewer never
  reads `AGENTS.md` / `.claude/rules/` and the steering is inert even with the
  collection fully synced.
- **Woods 1.3.0 fail-loud changes:** the index MCP raises `MissingArtifact`
  without embed artifacts unless `WOODS_ALLOW_AUTODETECT=1` (`bin/woods-start`
  defaults it on); the console MCP requires `config.console_mcp_enabled =
  true` (set in `config/initializers/woods.rb`).
- **The purge guard also fires on intentional mass removals.** Dropping a unit
  type from the sync set, changing `UNBLOCKED_REPO_URL`, or deleting a large
  swath of code can exceed the 30% deletion threshold — the sync warns and
  skips the purge. Run once with `UNBLOCKED_FORCE_PURGE=1` to apply it.
- **Profiles lag main by up to a day.** Reviews of PRs that build on
  same-day merges may cite slightly stale structure.

I have everything I need to lay out a solution. Here's what the investigation turned up.

## What's actually in place vs. what's missing

The woods-sync step lives in the **admin repo**, not this gem — currently on branch `claude/nice-mcclintock-5adaa6` (PR #13304, parent ENG-5434), being burned in with `soft_fail: true`. The step:

```yaml
- label: ":card_index: Sync Woods index to Unblocked"
  key: woods-sync
  if: build.branch == "main" && build.source == "schedule"   # nightly only
  commands:
    - bundle exec rails ci:setup --trace
    - bundle exec rails woods:extract
    - bundle exec rails woods:unblocked_sync
  artifact_paths:
    - "tmp/woods/**/*"     # uploads ~6.5k files; only ONE needs to persist
  soft_fail: true
```

The **upload half already works** — `artifact_paths` puts `unblocked_sync_manifest.json` into build artifacts every night. What's missing is pulling it back down at the *start* of the next run. Without it, each nightly run sees an empty `tmp/woods/`, so the gem's `SyncManifest` cold-starts and does a full ~800–1,200-call re-push.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The gem is already correct; this is purely a CI-plumbing gap.** `SyncManifest` self-heals — a missing, corrupt, or wrong-collection manifest is *discarded* and degrades to a full re-push. That's why "no manifest → full sync" (AC #2) needs zero gem code: the fallback is the gem's default behavior.
- **`build.source == "schedule"` gating means the manifest artifact only ever exists on scheduled builds** — so "restore from the last successful *scheduled* build" and "restore from the last passed build that has the artifact" are the same set. Simplifies discovery.
- **Buildkite artifacts are per-build and immutable; there's no built-in "latest" pointer.** Getting a *previous* build's artifact requires either discovering its build ID (REST API) or a cache plugin that abstracts that away.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## The one real decision: how to restore across builds

The ticket names two mechanisms. My investigation into the admin pipeline strongly favors the first:

**The admin pipeline has zero S3/cache-plugin infrastructure.** It uses only the `docker-compose` plugin plus a private Harbor registry for Docker layers — no `cache` plugin, no S3 bucket, no cross-build artifact download anywhere today. It also already has a clean secret-forwarding path: `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN/COLLECTION_ID/REPO_URL` are allowlisted in `.buildkite/ci-compose.yml` (lines 77–79), the same mechanism a Buildkite API token would use.

Given that:

**Recommended — Buildkite REST API + `buildkite-agent artifact download`:**
1. A pre-sync command queries the REST API for the last `passed` build on `main` → gets its build UUID.
2. `buildkite-agent artifact download "tmp/woods/unblocked_sync_manifest.json" tmp/woods/ --build <uuid>` — the *download* uses the agent access token (already mounted into the container by the docker-compose plugin), so only **build discovery** needs the new token.
3. Any failure (no token, no prior build, empty download) → `tmp/woods/` stays empty → gem does a full sync. Fully self-healing, matches AC #2.

- **Cost:** one new read-only Buildkite API token (scopes `read_builds` + `read_artifacts`), added to the existing ci-compose allowlist. Needs DevOps to register it as agent env, same as the Unblocked secrets.
- **Fit:** no new plugin, no bucket, no IAM — reuses patterns already in the pipeline.

**Alternative — S3-backed cache plugin** (e.g. `gencer/cache` or the official cache plugin): declarative restore/save keyed on a fixed key. Cleaner YAML, but requires standing up S3 + credentials + a plugin the repo doesn't use yet — more moving parts and more DevOps surface for one small file.

**Also in this same PR (AC #3):** narrow `artifact_paths` to just `"tmp/woods/unblocked_sync_manifest.json"` (reserve `dependency_graph.json` for ENG-5480). The doc explicitly says keep the broad `**/*` upload during the `soft_fail` burn-in for debugging, then narrow it *when the restore ships* — i.e. now.

**Verification (AC #4):** trigger two consecutive scheduled builds; the second should log `synced ~0 / skipped ~all`, proving a manifest hit rather than a cold re-push.

## The cadence note (secondary)

Once steady state is ~0 calls, per-merge syncing becomes viable (fresher review profiles than nightly). If you go per-merge, the step needs a Buildkite `concurrency_group` — **the gem does not lock the manifest**, so overlapping syncs would interleave manifest writes (the skill and doc both flag this as the host's responsibility). I'd treat this as a fast-follow after the restore is proven, not part of the restore PR.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
#
# Restore the Woods -> Unblocked sync manifest from the most recent passed
# scheduled build on main, so `woods:unblocked_sync` starts incremental
# (SyncManifest warm) instead of doing a cold full re-push.

require 'json'
require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
require 'fileutils'

ORG          = 'bigcartel'
MANIFEST_REL = 'tmp/woods/unblocked_sync_manifest.json'
API_HOST     = 'api.buildkite.com'

def log(msg) = warn("[restore-woods-manifest] #{msg}")

def bail(msg)
  log(msg)
  exit 0 # never fail the step; gem full-syncs on a missing manifest
end

# GET api.buildkite.com JSON with the Bearer token; returns parsed body or nil.
def api_get_json(path, token)
  uri = URI("https://#{API_HOST}#{path}")
  req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri)
  req['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{token}"
  res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port, use_ssl: true) { |http| http.request(req) }
  return nil unless res.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)

  JSON.parse(res.body)
rescue StandardError => e
  log("API GET #{path} failed: #{e.message}")
  nil
end

end
